method: One row per item of docs/parity/inventory-msg.json, same order and ids. For each item the implementing code was found by grepping custom_components/junghome_ble and tools/ for (a) the opcode constant bound to the item's opcode (jhmesh/config_messages.py CONFIG_*, jhmesh/messages.py GEN_*/LIGHT_*/SCENE_*/SENSOR_*/TIME_*/HEALTH_*, jhmesh/vendor_models.py JH_SCHEDULER_*/SCENE_ACTION_SETUP_*, messages._LBC_OPS for C2..D1 27 05, pdu.py proxy_config_*/FILTER_*), also as a raw hex literal (grep -rniE '0x<opcode>'), (b) the builder / decoder using that constant (def <name> in the same module) and (c) production callers of the builder/decoder (grep -rn '<builder>(' and register_status_handler(<CONST>) in coordinator.py, config_entities.py, sensor.py, mesh_config.py, schedules.py, commission.py, audit.py, tools/cli_ops.py, tools/mesh_poc.py) plus describe()/describe_config() dispatch entries (messages._describe, _SIG_GETS, _SIG_DESCRIBERS, config_messages._describe_params). Tests: an AST index of every tests/**/test_*.py function (names, attributes and string constants used in the body); a test counts for an item when it calls the item's builder/decoder or asserts on its wire hex / describe() text (checked by reading the test). Status rules: implemented = the app's behaviour for that message (encoding, ranges, reply matching) is reproduced by code that a listed test exercises; partial = message codec exists but a behaviour the app has for it is missing (no production caller where the JUNG layer has one, an extra-byte variant, a matching rule) or the only code is a describe() decoder for a message the app sends; gap = no builder and no decoder (describe() may still name it); na = not used. Items the inventory marks 'Library only' (Nordic class present, no JUNG-layer caller) are held to the same rule (the user asked for parity or better); a working builder+decoder+test counts as implemented, their absence as gap with feasibility. Line numbers are the first line matching a fixed regex per anchor (/tmp generator: A(file, regex)), so a rerun on the same tree reproduces them. Nothing was probed on air. Verification pass (adversarial): (1) every gap/partial row re-checked by grepping custom_components, tools and tests for the opcode as 0x<op>/<op> literals, the constant names, builder names (<snake name>( ), getattr/dir-based dispatch (only tools/mesh_sniff.py sig_property_opcodes, property ops) and the mesh_poc/cli_ops argparse sub-commands; no gap/partial row turned out implemented. (2) Rows were re-graded against this ledger's own rules: 'only a describe() decoder for a message the app sends' = partial (msg:op:8239 gap->partial), and 'codec exists but the JUNG layer has a read/wait path HA lacks' = partial, applied mechanically to every implemented row whose code refs are only jhmesh codec modules (messages/config_messages/vendor_models/pdu) while the inventory says the JUNG layer builds/decodes it, then checked for production callers by grep (msg:op:40, 8017, 823a implemented->partial; 41, 51, 801f, 8025, 8028, 8202/8203/8206/8207/824c/824d/825e, 8247, 829f have production or tools callers or an app-side flag-dependent branch and stay implemented). (3) Every code ref was checked to be a non-blank line of an existing file and every test ref to be an existing test function (AST); 16 implemented rows were read against the APK (03, 5c incl. W7/c TAI conversion, 8209, 00, 52 Format A/B, d42705-0 incl. 2-byte toggle form, d32705 vs AbstractC1934m0/C1937n0, 40, 41, 06, 8019, 822b, 8029, 8245, 8202, 04). Noted, not status-changing: 8202 production sends the 4-byte form with transition 0 (docs/ha-integration.md: deliberate) where the app sends 2 B; 52 Format B length is decoded per spec (+1) where the APK library omits the +1; 8209 accepts the full s32 range where the APK caps at s16. Citations: every `code` entry is now `path::symbol` (docs/parity/README.md, Row schema), converted from `path:line` by reading each line in the tree its ledger line was written against (git blame), following it through every later re-pointing that kept the cited text and past the merges that re-pointed lines to other code, and naming the innermost symbol holding it; `tools/parity.py check` verifies each symbol is defined.

rows.note: replies are matched on source + expected opcode (+ predicate), 3 attempts x 3 s per request (Model App Bind: 3 x 3 s where the app waits 3000 ms once). The app's substitute rule (any pending request completes on an LBC User Property Status D1 27 05 from the element, except an Admin Get/Set of 0x0009) is deliberately not reproduced: nodes publish D1 27 05 unsolicited (button events 0x5012, InsertId / KeyMode changes), so it would complete a Get or a command with an unrelated status and leave the state unknown; none of the 7-day captures shows a node answering a request that way. Its one effect that matters, a node that sent it not being marked unreachable, is kept: a node heard from while asked stays reachable (coordinator._missed_answer). Nor is the wait-less 0x8029 quirk reproduced

rows.note: An LBC Admin Property Status without a value - the property id and access byte (3 B), or the id alone (2 B: the metering socket's meter element answering the app's Admin Set of 0x5003 on air) - is dropped by _on_vendor_property_status and never clears a cached value, as the app's resolver drops it (AbstractC1972z0, UtilsKt.k). It still answers a pending request for its property id, as in the app, which neither resends nor reads back: PropertyReader.write returns 'not_supported' without a re-read, and the entity raises setting_not_supported. HA-idiomatic difference: the app moves on silently; HA reports that the device does not have the setting instead of showing a change that did not happen.

The app's other use of D1 27 05, as a substitute reply completing any pending request, is a waiting rule, tracked in msg:mech:waitforstatusmessage.

rows.reason: Declined: Home Assistant never narrows its proxy's filter. It keeps the empty reject list (receive everything) for a link's whole life (docs/dev/architecture.md, Behaviour worth knowing: the link sets the proxy filter to *blacklist, empty*) and commissions new nodes through that link (jhmesh/commission.py NOT_COVERED, first entry), so the app's address lists ({node, 0xFFFF, provisioner} during setup, {node, 0xFFFF} after) have no use. The builder exists and is tested, without the app's byte-cast quirk, but no flow sends it. Decision record: docs/roadmap.md, '### Candidates from the device side', 'Not worth doing' (review 4, report 6 §1), 'Proxy filter address lists'.
